claims.rule: For a cancellation bridge, trace the cancel token's evaluation through constructor strictness and executor switching. Keep the cancellation action suspended until it reaches the intended executor, propagate cancellation to the underlying fiber, and preserve the existing logger and finalizer observations.
claims.applicability: Observed in ZIO 2 RC-era Runtime.run and succeedBlocking in March 2022. Transferable review inference is to reason about both evaluation time and owner, not to mechanically replace eager constructors with lazy ones. In a current checkout, identify the replacement runtime/cancellation APIs and discover the effective executor configuration before testing.
claims.counterexample: An immutable snapshot of owner-confined state computed inside its owner's callback may need eager construction before passing the result to a foreign fiber. PR 8819 raised exactly that issue; blanket advice to make every expression lazy is wrong.
